name: DeepSeek V4 Flash DSpark — dual Spark, 1M context
statusNote: Runs now, but is not yet rankable. The engine blocker is GONE: this recipe served on stock vLLM 0.26.0 at --block-size 256 on 2026-07-28 via the flashinfer overlay (patches/flashinfer-dsv4-pbs256). What remains is the measurement contract, not the engine.

blockers.what: Whether greedy token identity survives an NCCL allreduce is still unmeasured. Now that the model actually serves, this is finally MEASURABLE on this target rather than theoretical — boot it twice under the pinned config and compare hashes.
blockers.sharedWith: glm-5-2-dual-spark-tp2 and every other dual-Spark recipe.
blockers.nextStep: Run the arena baseline against this target once multiNode is enabled in the contract.

blockers.what: ulimit -l is 8 MB on both nodes, so NCCL cannot use RDMA and falls back to sockets. It serves, but the interconnect is not running as the recipe intends, and a paired ratio measured over sockets is not the recipe's hardware.
blockers.nextStep: Root, once: raise memlock, then drop NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1.

blockers.what: oom-guard.sh trips at MemAvailable < 8192 MiB and killed a run that missed by 321 MiB, silently. The 6 GiB KV pin clears it, but the margin is thin and an arena arm must not die mid-measurement.
blockers.nextStep: Either raise the guard for arena runs or keep the KV pin at 6 GiB and verify headroom before each arm.

why: Worth scaffolding despite being blocked: at 1,048,576 tokens of context across two nodes with FP4 experts and FP8 dense, it exercises paths nothing else in the corpus does — and it is the recipe most likely to reward kernel work, because almost nothing on that path was written for sm_121.

served.note: First light, not a benchmark: --max-model-len 8192, NCCL over sockets because memlock is 8 MB, and there is no page-size-64 baseline to compare against because the model cannot run at 64 at all.
